# Pet Show and Tell

An Android Expo Go demo for introducing a pet, sharing an on-device photo post, browsing a sample pet feed, and reacting with Like or Love.

## Run locally

1. Install Node.js and npm.
2. Install dependencies with `npm install`.
3. Start Expo with `npm start`.
4. Open the project in a matching Expo Go app on an Android emulator.

The app uses Expo SDK 58, TypeScript, Expo Router, StyleSheet, Zustand, Expo SQLite, ImagePicker, and FileSystem. A matching SDK 58 version of Expo Go is required.

## Demo boundaries

- Seven pet profiles and nine photo posts are seeded locally from bundled assets.
- Your pets can be added and edited independently, and each post belongs to a selected pet.
- Profile, photo posts, and Like/Love reactions persist in SQLite on this device.
- Selected photos are copied into app-owned storage. Nothing is uploaded or shared with other devices.
- Comments, real accounts, public sharing, moderation, and backend storage are deferred.

## Tutorial routes

- `/` — pet feed and reactions
- `/pet-setup` — create or edit the local pet profile
- `/create-post` — choose a photo or sample and add a local post
- `/my-pet` — browse local pet profiles and their posts
- `/post/[id]` — post detail; comments are a planned follow-up
- `/exposition` — MDS package learning material

See `project/info.md`, `project/style.md`, `project/guidelines.md`, and `project/todo.md` for scope and project memory.

# Pet Show and Tell Guidelines

## Source of Truth
- Read project/info.md, project/todo.md, project/style.md, and this file before product or architecture changes.
- These project files hold product intent, roadmap, visual style, and technical rules.
- Ask before changing the local-only product boundary or adding a backend, account system, or public publishing.
- Keep the IDE reference folder read-only.

## Product Boundary
- First release is an Android Expo Go demo for one device.
- A static web export is in scope for the hosted i² phone-frame preview. It is session-only, same-origin, and not a public website. `npm run export:web` writes it; `PET_WEB_BASE_PATH` sets the sub-path.
- `eas.json` has an Android emulator APK profile. Store submission and iOS stay out of scope.
- The user creates one pet profile and local photo posts; seeded community-style posts are also shown.
- No sign-in, network API, public upload, shared storage, moderation service, or cross-device sync.
- Comments stay as an explicit tutorial-sized follow-up unless the owner updates the roadmap.
- Pet profiles use name, species, picture, and short description. Posts use pet ID, picture, description, and timestamp.
- Seed six pets and eight posts total, with some pets appearing in two posts.

## Expo Architecture
- Expo Router routes live under src/app.
- Keep route files thin and put screens, shared UI, fixtures, local persistence, and services in src/features, src/components, src/data, src/storage, and src/services.
- Use TypeScript and npm.
- Use React Native StyleSheet only; do not introduce Uniwind, NativeWind, or a second style system.
- Use Zustand for shared state across feed, detail, profile, and composer.
- Keep image selection on device and use an Expo-compatible image picker.
- Use local data and SQLite for on-device persistence. The web preview uses an in-memory session copy instead of SQLite, because the hosted frame has no cross-origin-isolation headers. Do not add remote calls.
- Do not add Expo UI, Native Tabs, authentication, or legal-document generation.
- EAS stays limited to the Android emulator APK profile. Do not submit to a store.
- Never put secrets in the app or EXPO_PUBLIC variables.

## Visual Direction
- Keep screens calm and photo-forward, with readable contrast and a friendly tone.
- Pet photos should be visually prominent.
- Use StyleSheet values consistent with project/style.md and project/theme.json.
- Include visible pressed/selected states for reactions, clear form validation, and accessible labels.
- Provide a bundled sample image path if photo-library permission is denied.

## Starter and Tutorial Code
- Treat exposition and stylist pages as temporary learning material; keep them until the tutorial phase is complete.
- Review project/todo.md and update task state as work is completed.
- Keep tutorial TODOs bite-sized, route/file-specific, and easy to verify by observation.
- Don't remove useful MDS onboarding, data, or settings examples without updating the ejection inventory.

## Workflow
- Use MDS guidance for project planning and app setup.
- This project uses Expo SDK 58. Before adding a package, check SDK 58 compatibility and use the Expo-compatible package version.
- After adding a package, install it with npm and capture any package-manager failure in the TODO.
- Use MDS Doctor and Expo Doctor when the owner asks for verification or when a tool reports a failed diagnostic that needs resolution.
- Do not claim a diagnostic passed unless its command output confirms it.
- Keep the generated test-to-main workflow documented for future repo work, but do not create branches unless requested.

## Safety and Public Sharing
- This milestone stores profile images and post images on device only.
- Never upload or publish user photos.
- Before adding public posting, plan authentication, shared storage, privacy, image rights, abuse reporting, and moderation.

# Pet Show and Tell Project Info

## App Name
Pet Show and Tell

## Overview
Pet Show and Tell gives pet owners a safe, friendly place to enjoy pictures of pets. The first implementation is an on-device Android demo of onboarding a pet, sharing a photo post, browsing a community-style feed, and reacting to posts. Nothing is published to a service.

## Target Users
Pet owners who want to create a profile for a pet, share pictures, and browse pictures of other people's pets.

## Problem this app solves
People who enjoy pets need a welcoming place to introduce their pets and browse pet photos. This milestone validates the first-time and feed experience before real public sharing is added.

## Product Goals
- Run in Expo Go on an Android emulator.
- Introduce the app, collect one local pet profile, and let the user add a photo post.
- Browse a community-style feed containing curated demo pets and the current device's own posts.
- Open post detail and toggle Like or Love.
- Keep implementation and remaining TODOs bite-sized and tutorial-friendly.

## Non-Goals
- No sign-in, account management, or remote identity.
- No backend, shared database, cloud media storage, public distribution, or cross-device sync.
- No moderation service, reporting, or notifications.
- No iOS, monetization, or store submission in this milestone.
- A static web export for the hosted i² preview, and an EAS Android emulator APK profile, are in scope. The web preview is not a public site and does not add a backend.
- Comments are a follow-up TODO for the prototype to complete, not part of the initial runnable flow.

## First User Flow
1. A multi-screen introduction explains creating a pet profile, sharing pictures of that pet, and browsing other people's pets.
2. The user can create multiple local pet profiles with a name, species, optional profile picture, and short description. A sample illustration remains available when no photo is selected.
3. The user adds a first photo post with a short description. The photo is selected from the device library and remains local.
4. The user enters the feed, browses seeded and locally created posts, opens post detail, and uses Like or Love.

## Core Flows and Features
- Multi-screen onboarding that hands off to local pet-profile creation.
- Create one local pet profile with name, species, optional picture, and short description.
- Create a local photo post associated with that pet; post fields are pet ID, picture, description, and timestamp.
- Browse the seeded feed plus posts created on this device.
- Open a post-detail screen.
- Like or Love a post; only one reaction can be selected at a time, and tapping it again clears it.
- Persist profile, posts, and reactions on device so they remain available while navigating and after restarting the app. The web preview keeps that state for the browser session only.
- Comments remain a Phase 2/prototype follow-up task. No network publishing.

## Screens
- Multi-screen onboarding.
- Pet profile setup.
- First photo-post composer using the device image library.
- Feed.
- Post detail with photo, description, and Like/Love reactions.
- Adding a comment list and composer is a tutorial-friendly TODO.
- No login/account screens, remote publishing UI, or moderation screens.

## Seed Data and Assets
- Seed six pets with at least one post each. Some pets may have a second post; use eight posts total.
- Each seeded pet has a name, species, picture, and short description.
- Each seeded post has pet ID, picture, description, and timestamp.
- The offline seed collection contains seven pet profiles and nine bundled local photos; keep asset paths easy to update.
- Newly created profile and post photos stay on device. Do not upload images.

## Data Needs
- Data mode: device-local Expo SQLite with Zustand shared state; no remote or server data. The web preview uses the same pet API in memory, seeded on each new tab, with an optional sessionStorage mirror.
- Local app state and device-local persistence only.
- Store one local pet profile, local posts, and the user's Like/Love reaction per post.
- Seed six pets and eight posts. Keep the data models and fixtures in files that can be edited without a backend.
- Use Expo SQLite for durable local records and Zustand for shared screen state.
- User-selected photos remain local to the device; there is no upload or external API.
- Expo SDK: 58; use versioned SDK 58 docs and SDK-matched Expo Go on Android.
- No accounts, shared database, real-time collaboration, analytics, or notifications.

## Platforms
- Target and first MVP platform: Android.
- Local preview: Android emulator through Expo Go.
- Hosted preview: `npm run export:web` writes a static Metro bundle to `dist-web/web`. `PET_WEB_BASE_PATH` sets the sub-path (default `/`). The portfolio serves that folder behind login. The i² frame supplies the phone chrome, so the web build does not draw its own status or navigation bar.
- No production release is planned.

## Release Strategy
The first version is an internal demo run locally in Expo Go on an Android emulator for prototype and tutorial use. A static web export can also be shown inside the hosted i² phone frame. It is not released through a store or public hosting.

## Monetization Strategy
No monetization planned.

## Team Context
One developer using MDS and beginner-friendly agent-guided tutorials. Remaining tasks should be independently actionable and have observable acceptance checks.

## Legal and Compliance Contact
No legal documents are generated for this local-only demo. Before real public publishing, decide business/contact details and review privacy, image rights, and moderation requirements.

## Later Scope and Possibilities
- Real accounts and a shared public community feed.
- Remote database and cloud image storage.
- Cross-device sync and public moderation/reporting.
- Comments, starting with a local comment list and composer as the tutorial follow-up.
These items are separate from the on-device demo and need product/security planning before release.

## Research, Notes, and References
- Product direction: a safe place for pet owners to enjoy pictures of pets.
- Planning/design reference: <local>/mrdj-dev-suite-i2Workspace/temp/Dual-Screen IDE Design-11-7-26. Read-only; do not modify.
- Product-specific pet photos have not yet been supplied; use local bundled examples/placeholders until they are added to the repo.
- Preserve the prototype journey: onboarding/profile, share a pet photo, browse feed, open detail, react; comments remain a follow-up.

## Tech Stack and MDS Setup
- Expo React Native, TypeScript, npm.
- Expo Router, routes under src/app.
- Android only, platform-specific files/layouts.
- React Native StyleSheet only; Zustand for shared app state.
- No auth/backend starter or separate API server.
- Local data mode; persist profile, posts, and reactions on device. No remote API calls.
- Use `expo-image-picker` for local photos and `expo-file-system` to copy them into app-owned storage; files remain on device. The web preview stores the chosen picture as a data URL in the session.
- No Expo UI or Native Tabs; preserve Expo Go compatibility.
- Multi-screen onboarding; handoff to pet setup and then the app.
- EAS is limited to the Android emulator APK profile. No legal-document generation or store deployment.
- Keep the MDS project/guidelines template and test-to-main safeguards.
- Do not save these selections as permanent personal defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Android Expo Go launches and onboarding completes without login.
- User can create multiple pet profiles with the defined fields; profile pictures are optional.
- User can select a device image or use a bundled sample and create a local photo post.
- Feed shows six seeded pets and eight seeded posts, plus the user's local post.
- Post detail displays the matching pet name, species, picture, and description.
- Like/Love state updates consistently and persists on device.
- Profile, posts, and reaction state remain local and can be restored after app restart.
- No user content is sent to a service.
- Comments remain an explicit TODO for the prototype to complete.

## Phase 0-2 Roadmap Intent
Phase 0 records this product and stack boundary. Phase 1 builds the app shell, onboarding/profile setup, local image selection, feed, and post detail. Phase 2 defines typed pet/post/reaction models, six local fixtures with eight posts, device-local persistence, and shared state actions. Leave comments and small tutorial-friendly polish tasks open for the prototype path. Each TODO should name the route or data file, describe an observable acceptance check, and give one direct next action.

# Pet Release Flow

## Test-To-Main Safeguards

- Build features on short-lived feature branches.
- Open pull requests into `test` first.
- Require the `MDS PR Checks` workflow to pass before merging into `test`.
- Smoke test the app from `test` with staging data and staging Supabase keys when Supabase is used.
- Promote from `test` to `main` only after validation.
- Protect `main` so direct pushes are blocked and PR checks are required.

## Supabase Environments

- Local dummy data is the starting point.
- When Supabase is introduced, create separate test/staging and production projects before wiring production data.

## GitHub Setup The User Still Needs To Do

- Create `test` and `main` branches.
- Confirm GitHub Actions is enabled for the repo and that the generated workflow is allowed to run.
- In GitHub branch protection, require pull requests and status checks for `test` and `main`.
- Require the generated `MDS PR Checks` workflow before merge.
- If the agent has GitHub access with enough permissions, let it apply these repo settings for you; otherwise do this one-time setup in the GitHub UI.

# Pet Show and Tell Style

## Visual Direction
Friendly, calm, and photo-forward. The app should feel welcoming to pet owners and keep each pet photo as the main focus. Prefer clear, uncluttered screens that work comfortably on a small Android phone.

## Brand and References
- Product language: safe place, enjoy pictures, share pet moments.
- The read-only IDE prototype folder is a workflow reference, not a visual reference for the pet app.
- No app-specific screenshots or brand assets have been supplied yet. Align the final styling to screenshots when available.

## Colors
- Use warm off-white backgrounds and quiet neutral surfaces.
- Use a calm green or teal as the main action color, with a warm coral accent for Love.
- Keep text dark and high contrast; never place text directly over busy images without a scrim.
- Keep color tokens in project/theme.json and provide readable light-mode surfaces.

## Typography
- Use the platform system font.
- Use a clear heading hierarchy and comfortable body text.
- Keep pet names prominent and descriptions readable; timestamps and secondary labels may be smaller but remain legible.

## Layout and Spacing
- Give photos generous space and use consistent rounded card corners.
- Use a single-column feed sized for phones.
- Keep primary actions reachable and visually distinct.
- Keep forms short, label fields clearly, and show validation beside the relevant field.

## Motion Tone
Subtle and cheerful. Use brief pressed-state feedback for cards and reaction buttons. Avoid motion that competes with the pet photos.

## Accessibility Notes
- Use readable contrast, scalable type, accessible labels for Like and Love, and visible selected states.
- Keep touch targets comfortable and ensure onboarding can be completed with screen-reader labels.
- Provide a sample-image path when photo-library permission is unavailable.

## Style Questions to Revisit
- Confirm exact palette and imagery after product-specific screenshots or pet photos are available.
